sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.6723 Of 2025
Order:

This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" ... to issue a Writ Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in forcefully trying to evict the petitioners from land admeasuring Ac. 0-20 gts in Sy. No. 1/39, Ac. 1-20 gts in Sy.
No. 18, Ac. 5-00 gts in Sy. No. 1/15, Ac. 0-20 gts in Sy. No. 1/40, Ac. 5-00 gts in Sy.
No. 1/15, of Pochampahad Village and land admeasuring Ac. 2-10 gts in Sy. No.
159/26 of Vempally Village, Hajipur Mandal, Mancherial District and taking signatures on the Blank Agreement high handedly without there being any Notification issued under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act 2013, as contemplated under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition. Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and consequently direct the respondents not to compel the petitioners to sign on the blank agreement without there being any preliminary notification as required under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act 2013 as the same is illegal, arbitrary and violative of Article 19.
21 and 300-A of Constitution of India and Contrary to the provisions of Land Acquisition Act 2013 not to interfere with the peaceful possession over the subject property."

2. Heard Sri B.Shiva Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for respondent Nos.1 to 4.
3.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the writ petition is being disposed of at the stage of admission.

4. Facts giving rise to filing of this writ petition briefly stated are that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of the agricultural land to an extent of Ac.0-20 gts., Ac.1-20 gts., Ac.0-20 gts.,
Ac.5-00 gts,. and Ac.0-10 gts., in Sy.Nos.1/39, 1/18, 1/40, 1/15 and 159/26, situated at Pochampahad Village and Vempally Village, Hajipur Mandal, Mancherial Distrcit (herein after referred to as "subject property") and as per the final patta certificates issued by the then Tahsildar,
their names were mutated in the revenue records and pattadar passbooks and title deeds were issued in their favour.

While things stood thus, respondent Nos.2 to 4 came to the subject property of the petitioners on 11.02.2025 and tried to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property,
without issuing any notice and without following due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'Act 30 of 2013') and the action of respondent Nos.2 to 4 is gross violation of provisions of the Act 30 of 2013 and also violative of Article 300-A of the Gajelli Laxmi vs The State Of Telangana on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150466837/
1 constitution of India.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that if the subject property of the petitioners is required for public purpose, respondents ought to have follow the due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013 and pay compensation to the petitioners, then only respondents are entitled to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property and on the other hand respondents are insisting the petitioners for executing agreements as per Rule 14 of the Rules framed under the Act 30 of 2013.

6. Per contra, learned Assistant Government Pleader submitted that as on today, respondent authorities have not issued any notification and if the subject property of the petitioners is required for public purpose, respondent authorities will follow the due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013.
He further submitted that the petitioners have approached this Court and filed present writ petition with an apprehension and the same is liable to be dismissed on the ground of being pre-mature.

7. Having considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties and after perusal of the material available on record, it reveals that petitioners are claiming right over the subject property,
pursuant to the final patta certificates issued by the then Tahsildar and their names were mutated in the revenue records and pattadar passbooks and title deeds were issued in their favour.

8. Taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions made by the respective parties, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the Writ Petition, with a direction to respondent Nos.2 to 4 not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property without following due procedure as contemplated under law.

It is needless to observe that if the subject property of the petitioners is required for public purpose, respondent Nos.2 to 4 ought to have follow due procedure as contemplated under the Act 30 of 2013.
9. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
There shall be order as to costs.

Note: Issue CC in three days b/o vsl Gajelli Laxmi vs The State Of Telangana on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150466837/
